items.title: Richard Scolyer, who challenged the world to 'be brave, be bold', dies aged 59
items.description: The 2024 Australian of the Year, Richard Scolyer, has died. In his final message he urged all Australians to "pursue their dreams and passion with humility, love and compassion".

items.title: Live: Iran fires missiles at Israel's north as a 'warning' after strikes in Beirut
items.description: The strikes from Iran are the first such bombardment since a fragile ceasefire took effect in early April. Follow live.

items.title: Iran briefing: Day 100 of this war ends in a way we all saw coming
items.description: This was day 100 of this war, and it's left us with a tinderbox which could be about to explode, writes our correspondent Matthew Doran.

items.title: When a detective told a witness Joanna was pregnant, she took police to VCAT
items.description: A woman who says she suffered life-changing stress and anxiety — and later, the death of one of her babies — after a Victoria Police officer unlawfully disclosed that she was pregnant wants her story known.

items.title: Tasmania's population boom has gone bust — and it spells trouble
items.description: From being a hot destination 10 years ago, Tasmania's population growth has ground to a halt — and big changes will be needed to reverse the trend, experts say.

items.title: Top neurologists say regulator ignored warnings as weed killer decision looms
items.description: Australia's leading movement disorder specialists say the chemical regulator has not engaged with their concerns about paraquat, despite growing evidence linking the herbicide to Parkinson's disease.

items.title: 'We blinked': Government accused of backing down on AI regulation
items.description: The world's biggest tech titans see Australia as a promising investment opportunity for their AI ambitions, but some fear the federal government's regulatory retreat could cause more harm.

items.title: Anthropic wants caution but the market wants more AI
items.description: Anthropic wants caution as AI intelligence surges but the stock market can't get enough.

items.title: From migration to AUKUS, more politicians are speaking out
items.description: Former Coalition frontbencher Paul Scarr says inflammatory migration rhetoric is taking a toll on migrant communities. His warning comes as both major parties wrestle with populist pressures.

items.title: Live: Reece Walsh recalled as Maroons reveal Game II team
items.description: Queensland coach Billy Slater reveals his team for State of Origin II, with injuries forcing a reshuffle for the Maroons ahead of their must-win clash at the MCG. Follow live.

items.title: The electric classic car that now drives like a 'pocket rocket'
items.description: It may look like a small vintage car, but an EV conversion has brought it "up to speed" to its modern counterparts.

items.title: Maths genius, devoted mum, headline-making CEO on King's Birthday Honours roll
items.description: Almost 950 Australians are honoured, including five stand-out recipients who are now Companions of the Order.

items.title: The Top End town where 15 people died preventable deaths in six months
items.description: Remote Indigenous communities across Australia are painfully aware that their life expectancy rates are worsening — and in one Northern Territory community, residents are calling for an investigation into a local death rate they feel is "not normal".

items.title: Does being in a 'safe seat' influence whether your hospital gets an upgrade?
items.description: Are hospitals in safe seats being overlooked for multi-million-dollar refurbishments by the Victorian government?

items.title: With his pet chihuahua and trusty gopher, 97yo grazier won't slow down
items.description: At 97, Doug Harrison still scoots around his outback station on a gopher, doing as much work as he can. As he nears a century of living, he reflects on memorable moments over the decades, with a cuppa in hand and his trusty chihuahua by his side.

items.title: History quiz: When was the first Mars Exploration Rover launch?
items.description: What make of car was stolen in the world's first official vehicle theft? And do you know where the Endeavour was repaired after hitting the Great Barrier Reef in 1770?

items.title: Shrek, Captain Cook and the stars: Welcome to Brian Robinson's multiverse
items.description: Newcastle Art Gallery presents the distinctive and intricate work of the Torres Strait Islander artist in its first major solo survey following a four-year refurbishment.

items.title: Why sentiment in Japan has turned against foreigners despite a worker shortage
items.description: Japan's answer to One Nation skyrocketed in popularity after adopting an anti-immigration stance despite Japan needing foreign workers more than ever.

items.title: Quick hits: Monaco GP interrupted for safety as Kardashians keep up with F1
items.description: From a dodgy section of track to a mega celebrity watching her partner equal a record with the great Ayrton Senna, the 2026 Monaco Grand Prix had plenty of talking points.

items.title: Piastri promoted after penalty as teen sensation wins wild Monaco GP
items.description: Teenage sensation Kimi Antonelli was flawless to lead every lap of a drama-filled Monaco Grand Prix, claiming a fifth consecutive win to extend his lead in the Formula 1 drivers' championship. Follow live.

items.title: Zverev claims first major with French Open victory
items.description: In his fourth appearance in the final of a major tournament, Alexander Zverev lifts the French Open trophy following a five-set grind against Flavio Cobolli.

items.title: Aussies crowned rugby sevens world champions after conquering NZ
items.description: Maddison Levi ignores a knee injury to score a superb double as Australia wraps up the women's rugby sevens World Championship in France.

items.title: Outback cake decorator stops reporting vandalism because 'nothing gets done'
items.description: After three vandalism incidents in three years, cake decorator Ishani Harney says the emotional and financial toll of crime lingers long after the damage is repaired.

items.title: Victorian teachers sue over alleged unpaid superannuation
items.description: A class action alleges the Education Department short-changed teachers some $100 million in superannuation contributions between 1995 and 2023.

items.title: Qld government contemplates ditching anti-junk-mail measures
items.description: A new consultation paper argues the measures are too burdensome and recommends repealing state laws and making local councils responsible for combating junk mail.
